S001@7611-7692.words: do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work
S001@7611-7692.reason: The judgement says nearly all studies in the source had low confidence in their findings, which affects how far a reader can trust the evidence on whether these programmes work.

S001@7900-8058.reason: The judgement describes why children with disabilities fall behind, which is background on the gap; it gives no evidence on whether any intervention improves their education or which kinds work best.

S001@8059-8153.reason: The judgement concerns interventions to equalise health outcomes, whereas the question asks about educational outcomes for children with disabilities, so it does not bear on whether education programmes work.

S001@8154-8406.reason: The judgement recommends a twin-track approach combining disability-specific support with mainstream inclusion (teacher skills, accessibility), which bears on which kinds of programmes work best for children with disabilities.

S001@8407-8703.reason: The judgement says most evaluated interventions targeted individual children rather than school- or system-level mainstreaming, which shapes how a reader should weigh the evidence on which kinds of programmes work best.

S001@8704-8859.reason: The judgement says evaluation should focus on interventions that target both the individual with a disability and their wider environment, which bears on which kinds of education programmes for children with disabilities are best supported by evidence.
